# Rear tailgate catch adjustment for noise reduction

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Adjust the rear tailgate catch inward up to 4mm and retighten screws. [t55]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Take a quick drive down the highway to hear the current noise level.
2. Grab your T-40 torx bit and pop open the rear hatch.
3. [Partial] Loosen two specific torx screws on the tailgate catch mechanism.
4. [Partial] Adjust the rear tailgate catch inward as far as it will go, using a wrench handle if necessary to move it 2-4mm.
5. Retighten the previously loosened torx screws.

_Procedure reported by [t55]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-reduce-interior-wind-and-road-noise-free.1545/>_

## Tools

- T-40 torx bit [t55]

## Tips & gotchas

- Adjust the catch as far in as possible, using a wrench to tap it if stuck. [t55]
- Move the latch approximately 2-4mm inward for best results. [t55]
